sampling_model.design: An independent sample \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\) is drawn from the selected multinomial law \(q\); an optional COPAG confidence set is produced from the same sample by a coverage-valid discovery procedure.
sampling_model.units: Each sampled unit is one retained clinical visit with finite coded variables \(V\); the population SCM also contains the binary selection variable \(S\).
sampling_model.treatment: The causal query is the hard intervention \(do(B=b)\); the intervention is hypothetical and sampling randomness comes from the selected observational sample.
sampling_model.overlap: Every selected cell is positive under \(q\). The common lower bound \(\delta\) on population and post-intervention selection is a calibrated sensitivity restriction, not a standard overlap label; the conditional estimand itself only requires \(d_M>0\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Estimate \(q\) by a simultaneous multinomial confidence region and propagate graph uncertainty by union over a COPAG confidence set; no faithfulness assumption is imposed on the identification class.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 equates a fixed canonical-DAG discrete causal bounding problem with minimization and maximization of a polynomial program.
Theorem 3 states that optimal neural counterfactual bounds and optimal PAG counterfactual bounds coincide under a faithful observational law.
Theorem 4.13 gives equality of marginal DAG models for DAGs with the same latent projection, and Proposition 7.3 commutes intervention with projection.
Proposition 2 replaces one latent source by at most \(d+1\) values without changing the observed network behavior.
Equality of selected-marginalized directed graphs is equivalent to indistinguishability under the Observe-and-Do probing scheme.
Theorem 4.15 gives completeness of sIDP and the causal calculus for unconditional interventional kernels under a COPAG.
Theorem 5 states that faithful distributions are nonempty, open, and dense in the total-variation Markov model.
Criterion inversion yields consistent set estimators, rates, and confidence regions for identified sets defined by population minimizers.
Width-adaptive endpoint intervals attain uniform asymptotic coverage for an interval-identified scalar as the identification width approaches zero.
Resampling and screening followed by a union of graph-specific intervals gives asymptotic coverage for a fixed causal effect after causal discovery.

body.tldr: A positive selected law need not be faithful, and exact graphical strata are open because an actual parent or shared source can disappear when a response mass approaches zero. The project indexes every primitive functional-essentiality feature by directed vertex pairs and invariant source child sets, proves that explicit nonnegative polynomial signs are equivalent to the exact selected MAG even when dependence occurs only at off-support endogenous inputs, and compiles bounded finite response strata. A certified procedure enumerates at most \(N!\,2^{N(N-1)/2+2^N-1}\) architectures and returns either an algebraic legal endpoint witness or a cell certificate excluding every enumerated legal lift. Universal legal lifting for arbitrary positive, potentially unfaithful selected laws remains the open kernel. The population and post-intervention \(\delta\) margins are calibrated sensitivity restrictions, while inference is limited to finite-sample outer coverage. The saturated binary case has the attained sharp interval \(\left[1/20,39/40\right]\), providing a regression test and an audit target for the survivor-selected cardiac-surgery analysis of Lee et al.

project_justification.gap: Chen and Mooij give complete point identification for COPAGs under selection, Yang et al. optimize over PAG-compatible neural SCMs under faithfulness, and Duarte et al. give sharp polynomial programs for a fixed canonical DAG. None characterizes closure or attainment after imposing the actual, rather than merely permitted, selected-MAG stratum for a positive but potentially unfaithful selected law.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is the graph-legal compatibility fiber: a finite union of semialgebraic response-function strata whose invariant essential-feature signs determine the selected MAG and whose boundary losses are either repaired by an equal-moment legal lift or exposed by a negative certificate.
project_justification.fill: The project supplies an invariant essential-feature index and an if-and-only-if polynomial legality lemma, a bounded finite stratum compiler, and a certificate-producing architecture-enumeration procedure. It isolates universal graph-legal lifting as the load-bearing open question, resolves its compelled-collider kill test first, and retains finite-sample confidence-fiber coverage without asserting endpoint convergence.

body.related_work: Richardson and Spirtes define maximal ancestral graphs under latent marginalization and selection conditioning. Evans's Theorem 4.13 canonicalizes latent DAG margins and Proposition 7.3 makes latent projection commute with intervention, but these results identify model equivalence rather than closure of an exact functional-essentiality stratum. Carey et al. characterize selected interventional indistinguishability by selected-marginalized directed graphs; their normalized selected models do not fix the absolute natural and interventional selection probabilities used for sensitivity calibration here. Rosset, Gisin, and Wolfe's Proposition 2 gives sourcewise Carathéodory reduction, while the exclusive-or diagnostic shows why moment preservation alone can destroy an actual shared source. Duarte et al.'s Proposition 1 and Theorem 1 give finite full-response disturbance models and polynomial sharp bounds for a fixed canonical DAG; the present work is informed by that encoding and adds an invariant exact-MAG sign test and negative certificates across all enumerated COPAG architectures. Yang et al. characterize PAG-compatible SCMs under faithfulness but do not treat selection or zero-mask closure. Chen and Mooij give complete COPAG point identification under selection and leave sharp discrete bounds open. Boeken, Forré, and Mooij establish openness and density of faithful laws, which does not supply an equal-moment lift on an unfaithful boundary. Chernozhukov, Hong, and Tamer, Imbens and Manski, and Chang, Guo, and Malinsky inform confidence-set inversion; the formal inference result here is only finite-sample outer coverage. Lee et al. provide the clinical consumer: FCI and LV-IDA are applied after conditioning on discharge alive, with acknowledged selection bias and graph ambiguity.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The binary exclusive-or family in the moment-compression warning holds the positive selected law and intervention moment fixed while a common-source edge disappears at both support boundaries. Thus an individual graph-legal parameter stratum is not closed, and moment-preserving support deletion is not a proof of exact-graph compactness. This diagnostic is not a claim that the fiber endpoint is unattained, because the same boundary moments have a distinct legal lift.
body.honest_scope: Source merging by identical child set, moment-preserving finite support on a fixed permitted architecture, exact polynomial legality for a finite response model, the saturated interval, certified feasibility within the bounded architecture list, and finite-sample confidence-set event inclusion are theorem targets. Equality between arbitrary selected SCMs and the bounded exact-stratum compiler, preservation of unnormalized selection probabilities through canonicalization, and universal graph-legal lifting for positive unfaithful \(q\) remain open. No general Hausdorff, Painlevé--Kuratowski, or endpoint-convergence claim is made. If the compelled-collider test produces an unattained endpoint certified outside every legal architecture, compactness is withdrawn and the certified attainment frontier is the main result. Under a complete all-circle COPAG the formula reduces to bounded-outcome missing-selection logic; for a vacuous intervention it reduces to \(\mathbb E_q[h(A)]\).
